parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime imposes universal, inescapable exposures: every trans visitor's documents are processed under a national regime issuing passports by assigned sex, with X markers blocked, confiscations/strandings documented, and an entry cable directing refusal where officers doubt an applicant's sex, with potential lifetime fraud ineligibility. In this state, facility use per identity is banned and criminalised under a trespass statute, with a documented arrest and 24-hour holding in a men's ward — birth-sex custody placement. Custody abuses nationally are severe (forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse, conversion-style policies). A travelling family faces a 10-year provider felony blocking minors' care plus investigation exposure. Recourse is thin: no statewide nondiscrimination or gender-identity hate-crime coverage; litigation unresolved. No documented pathway to routine imprisonment or execution of visitors, keeping this below the 0.15 tier, but documented arrest, entry refusal and custody harm place it firmly in High Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports issued by assigned sex; X markers blocked; passports confiscated/blocked, travellers stranded; entry cable instructs refusal where sex is doubted and consideration of permanent fraud ineligibility; foreign governments issued travel advisories after detentions of citizens over visa issues.
entry_documents.protection: Suit against the passport policy unresolved; existing X passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry can escalate into fraud suspicion, secondary investigation and detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented arrest of a trans woman under the bathroom law, handcuffed and held 24 hours in a men's ward; national corrections bureau mandates conversion-style policies for trans inmates; immigration custody shows forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men; reporting on trans prisoner counts stopped.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; employment circuit precedent since 2011.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A facilities encounter escalates to arrest, then birth-sex custodial placement; visa doubt can convert to immigration detention.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State bans facility use per gender identity in schools (2022) and extended bans through 2024; SB 79 declares an immutable binary; this state is among those criminalising restroom use in certain circumstances, with one documented arrest under its trespass law.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Trespass offence requires willful entry and refusal to depart when asked, with exemptions (chaperoning, emergencies); the exposure is not automatic arrest on entry.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National executive order bars congruent facility use in government-funded single-sex facilities, reinforcing the state ban.

care_services.exposure: Class C felony (10 years) for providers giving puberty blockers, hormones or surgery to anyone under 19, enforceable since 2023 and surviving challenge; proposed national rules would bar public insurance reimbursement for under-18 care; no insurance-exclusion ban or state-employee trans benefits.
care_services.protection: Adult care access is not documented as restricted in this state.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor needing continuity of care is denied it; the accompanying parent faces investigation-adjacent exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ memo uses 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist framings; EO directs prosecution of teachers facilitating minors' transitions; subpoenas of hospitals for minors' records; rescinded prison protections.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders blocked or enjoined; the memo states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State threat-framing licenses street-level and institutional hostility and raises outing consequences.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care ban with provider felony; school bathroom mandates by birth certificate; school sports bans K-12 and college; national EO targeting schools and teachers; shutdown of LGBTQ youth crisis services; proposed insurance bar.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian's travel with a trans minor risks care denial, missed schooling and state inquiry even without the guardian committing an offence.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented trans-specific incidents in the state; a killing rate of 3.8/100k is an undercount floor without denominators, so violence magnitude is not assessable; hate-crime law excludes gender identity; no statewide public-accommodations recourse.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute and circuit employment precedent exist but are not shown operating locally.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absent local recourse, a victim reporting assault may face outing through ID checks.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide nondiscrimination law, no hate-crime coverage for gender identity, courts in this circuit upholding document refusals; oversight litigations unresolved, so operative rules shift without notice.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation, legal-aid FAQ resources, and two municipal nondiscrimination ordinances; national equality protections remain on paper.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse operates mostly ex post and outside this state; a short-stay visitor cannot realistically use it.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.15-C documents routine street sweeps, coerced statements and prolonged abusive detention of visitors as organised targeting. This jurisdiction documents arrest (trespass, 60 days), harsh custody if detained, and entry refusal, but no pattern of sweeps or routine imprisonment of visitors — materially less severe, hence above 0.15.

0.25-C features birth-sex prison housing and a cross-dressing statute with brief sentences. This jurisdiction matches the custody-by-birth-sex exposure and adds universal document screening at the border, a criminalised facilities statute with a documented arrest, and a provider felony affecting travelling minors — a heavier combined regime, so it sits above 0.25.

0.35-A's universal border-exposure register with exclusion and no remedy parallels the entry-cable and passport regime here. But this jurisdiction adds state facility criminalisation with a documented arrest, birth-sex ward placement, custody abuse, and minors' care bans, so it rates below 0.35.

0.75-C shows brief detention, functioning tribunals, compensation and trained officers. Here remedies are thin or absent, courts in the circuit uphold document refusals, an arrest under a bathroom law was documented, and custody placement is by birth sex — the opposite direction of every 0.75 feature.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines a national document/entry apparatus that makes every trans visitor's passport itself an exposure (assigned-sex issuance, blocked X markers, strandings, refusal instructions with fraud-ineligibility risk) with a state layer that criminalises identity-congruent facility use and has produced a documented arrest and men's-ward custody. If detention occurs, documented national custody abuse (forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse, conversion-style policies) sets the worst case high, though it requires a detention trigger. Families travelling with minors face a separate, concrete exposure: a 10-year provider felony forecloses care continuity and invites investigation-adjacent scrutiny. Threat-framing at national counterterrorism level amplifies hostility. Against this, protections are mostly paper or out-of-state: hate-crime coverage nationally, unresolved litigation, two municipal ordinances. No documented execution pathway keeps the score above the 0.15 tier; the universal exposures, criminalised facilities, documented custody harm and thin recourse hold it in the mid-High-Risk band.
